articles.title: TIMELINE: Changes in AFP’s structure since revised modernization law
articles.summary: Here’s a breakdown of major changes in the military’s organization and structure since the Revised AFP Modernization Act was signed in 2012

blocks.text: It has been nearly 14 years since then-president Benigno Aquino III signed the Revised Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) Modernization Act, a landmark law that enabled the military not only to acquire modern assets but also to review its structure and personnel.
Many of the adjustments reflect the Philippines’ goal of shifting its focus from internal security operations to territorial defense.
Here’s a breakdown of how the AFP’s organizational structure has shifted since then:

The first AFP Modernization Act is signed. Aside from acquisition of assets, the plan includes components on force restructuring and organizational development as well as human resource development. The latter puts emphasis on the need for the AFP to transition from an internal security-oriented force to a primarily external security-oriented force.
But reluctance from Congress to fund it, as well as the 1997 Asian financial crisis, prevented the plan from taking off, a 2005 paper by defense expert Renato de Castro said.
The law’s implementation period lapsed 15 years later in February 2010.

The AFP’s six-year Internal Peace and Security Plan — more commonly known as Oplan Bayanihan — takes effect. It aims to eventually allow the AFP to transition into a territorial defense-focused force.

From 2011 to 2013, the AFP continued its primary task of fighting internal armed threats. The remaining years — 2014 to 2016 — were focused on handing over the lead role in internal peace and security to appropriate civilian agencies.

The Defense Planning Guidance (2013–2018) is released, according to a 2016 study by De Castro. It restructures the AFP into a “lean but fully capable” military to confront the challenges to the country’s territorial integrity and maritime security. The guide emphasizes the importance of naval assets.
The guide also includes the reduction of infantry and marine battalions so limited financial resources could be redirected to key priorities. These reductions would take effect in 2012.

The military’s development arm and anti-insurgency unit, the National Development Support Command, is abolished. It was first formed in 2006 under the Arroyo government to handle the military’s development programs in far-flung areas and address insurgency.
The AFP National Capital Region Command (NCRCOM) is deactivated. It had mainly served as an anti-coup unit in the capital region.
A smaller joint military task force for Metro Manila is activated to take NCRCOM’s place, called the Joint Task Force (JTF) NCR.

Aquino signs the Revised AFP Modernization Act. It effectively restarts the clock on the modernization program, but also amends the language used to describe the components on force restructuring and human resource development.
The revised law says the AFP should be transformed into a “multi-mission oriented force” that has the shifting capability to meet internal and external threats.

Responsibility for Bajo de Masinloc (Scarborough Shoal), a high-tide elevation some 120 nautical miles off Zambales, is transferred from the Tarlac-based Northern Luzon Command (Nolcom) to the Palawan-based Western Command (Wescom).
The move is meant to put the country’s external defense efforts under one commander. Wescom also has more ships and aircraft capable of monitoring the shoal.
The Philippine Navy activates its Submarine Group to “lay the groundwork for undersea warfare.”

Special operations are effectively unified under one command, after then-president Rodrigo Duterte deactivated the Army Special Operations Command and transferred its personnel to the newly activated AFP Special Operations Command (AFPSOCOM).

The AFPSOCOM is tasked with commanding all the military’s elite units: the Special Operations Wing of the Air Force, Naval Special Operations Group of the Navy, Scout Ranger Regiment, Special Forces Regiment (Airborne) and Light Reaction Regiment of the Army, and Joint Special Operations Group of the General Headquarters.
The AFP activates the AFP Cyber Group (AFPCyG).

Duterte signs Republic Act No. 11709, which sets a fixed three-year term for high-ranking AFP officers, including the chief of staff. The law is said to end a “revolving door” policy that gave rise to military chiefs serving for only a few months before mandatory retirement.
Other provisions in the law intend to strengthen the merit system of the AFP and ensure continuity of programs and policies.

The 4th Marine Brigade transfers from Sulu to Ilocos Norte. It is now under the command of Nolcom, which means it is also responsible for Scarborough Shoal and the Philippine Rise, key features in the West Philippine Sea. (READ: From Sulu to Burgos, the Marines’ Fourth Brigade comes home)

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. amends the law fixing high-ranking AFP officers’ terms to three years. The AFP chief is given a “maximum tour of duty” of three consecutive years, instead of the “fixed tour of duty” in the previous law.
The maximum tour of duty of the commanding generals of the Army, Navy, and Air Force are also set to two years instead of the three stipulated in the law Duterte signed.
The AFP reactivates its counterintelligence group that is tasked with protecting the military against espionage, sabotage, and other intelligence activities.

The unit was first organized in 1989 and disbanded in 1995 to create a presidential task force on intelligence and counterintelligence instead. (READ: Why did the Philippines reactivate its military counterintelligence group?)
Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. announces that the AFP is embarking on a “comprehensive archipelagic defense concept.” It is the country’s strategy to secure its vast maritime areas.

A new AFP Intelligence Command is activated “to enhance the nation’s intelligence capabilities in response to evolving security challenges,” according to AFP spokesperson Colonel Francel Margareth Padilla.
The AFPCyG becomes the AFP Cyber Command sometime in late 2024. Expanding the group into a command allows it to have more personnel and equipment. (READ: AFP chief Brawner eyes ‘Cyber Command’)
JTF NCR once again becomes the NCRCOM.

The reorganization of the Naval Forces West to the Western Naval Command and the Naval Forces Northern Luzon to the Northern Luzon Naval Command is approved. (READ: Presence is deterrence: The Philippine Navy’s pivot)

The AFP reorganizes special operations again, deactivating the AFPSOCOM and simultaneously reactivating the Special Operations Command of the Philippine Army and creating the Joint Special Operations Command of the AFP.

The AFP officially activates the AFP Strategic Command. It is described as a “strategic hub where intelligence, operations, and civil-military functions converge,” and is tasked with overseeing and synchronizing joint exercises and engagements with allies and partners.
The AFP announces plans for a space force or a space command by 2028. – Rappler.com

articles.title: In Philippines’ external defense push, resilience boils down to logistics
articles.summary: As the Revised AFP Modernization Act approaches the end of its 15-year horizon, what upgrades are in store for the Philippine military?

image.caption: The modernization program at a glance

blocks.text: Special Report
As the Revised AFP Modernization Act approaches the end of its 15-year horizon, what upgrades are in store for the Philippine military?
MODERN FLEET. The BRP Tarlac (LD-601) sails in waters close to Bajo de Masinloc (Scarborough Shoal) alongside partner navies for an ADMM-Plus joint sail in September 2026.

SUBIC, Philippines – When visiting the Philippine Navy’s newest warships at the Naval Operating Base (NOB) in Subic, most people — including military personnel — go through at least three gates. The long wait at the first gate speaks volumes of how the vision of a modern armed forces turns into reality.

Despite its ambitions, the Navy does not have its own docking facility to accommodate its brand-new frigates and offshore patrol vessels (OPVs). The big shipyard here that holds the country’s finest warships is owned by private firm Agila Subic Compass, which assigns its own civilian security at the first two gates that visitors enter.
Yet, what a sight to behold — a fleet of six modern gray ships now owned by a navy of an archipelago that had, for decades, had to make do with hand-me-downs from its allies.
READ State of PH Navy modernization: ‘Golden days will return’

In August when we paid a visit one damp and humid evening, we saw the BRP Diego Silang (FFG-07) berth at the shipyard after almost a week out at sea for a maritime patrol and joint drills with Australia and the United States. Already docked beside the spot allocated for her was a fleet of the Navy’s pride — modern frigates that were acquired, in relative rapid succession, under the Revised Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) Modernization Act.

Silang docked beside her sister ship, the BRP Miguel Malvar, which was commissioned in the summer of 2025. With them were two similar ships, BRP Jose Rizal and BRP Antonio Luna, the first brand-new frigates that the Navy acquired in 2020 and 2021 after a long wait. Before this, the Navy had to live with old ships from other countries which it would refurbish.
Flanking the frigates were the modern fleet’s first and latest acquisitions.

The BRP Tarlac, an Indonesia-made landing platform dock, was the first major vessel to be delivered in 2016 under the new modernization program. Beside it stood a similar ship, the BRP Davao del Sur. Both Tarlac and Davao del Sur are the largest of the Navy’s vessels that perform a wide array of tasks — humanitarian and disaster response, as well as resupply missions for features in the West Philippine Sea.

Beside Tarlac was the BRP Ramon Alcaraz, a US coast guard cutter commissioned to the Philippines in 2013. She’s a senior citizen in human years, but remains a steady and reliable workhorse for the fleet, especially for maritime patrols in all fronts of the country’s maritime spaces.
On the other side of the lineup was the freshly commissioned BRP Rajah Lakandula, an OPV. It was the first to berth at the Naval Station Jose Andrada in Manila, after dredging work in the area.
Reality check

That the Philippine Navy’s newest and most modern platforms are docked in a private facility in Subic, where the government must pay fees for usage, illustrates the difficulties the AFP continues to face despite strides in modernization since 2012.

The privately owned NOB-Subic is still the largest port facility for the Navy. The waters off the Naval Station Heracleo Alano in Cavite (popularly known as Sangley Point) are far too shallow for the newest assets of the Philippine Fleet.

This is why the defense department is looking to finally acquire and convert some 300 hectares of the state-owned Philippine Veterans Investment Development Corporation (Phividec) Industrial Estate in Tagoloan, Misamis Oriental, into a naval base that will include drydock facilities. However, over a year since Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. confirmed that the department was proceeding with the planned acquisition, talks have yet to wrap up.
READ Teodoro says Misamis Oriental will be center of Navy ops in Northern Mindanao, Visayas
A rusty past
Things were vastly different a dozen years ago.

Then-military chief Gregorio Catapang Jr. recalled that in one naval gunfire exercise, rust icicles would fall on the beddings of sailors inside a hand-me-down battleship. At the time, the Navy’s newest vessel was the BRP Conrado Yap, a secondhand corvette from the South Korean Navy. Before her were the secondhand vessels from the US, the Del Pilar class.
Today, more vessels are coming — mostly brand-new ones, although both Japan and South Korea are also set to transfer their existing five and two warships each.

The Indonesia-made BRP Tarlac and BRP Davao del Sur, named after the home provinces of the presidents under whom they were commissioned, will soon be joined by the BRP Ilocos Norte and the BRP Leyte. At least four more OPVs of the BRP Rajah Sulayman class will be delivered to the Philippines, and the BRP Diego Silang will eventually be joined by two more sister ships.
Senior officers of the military are not one to take for granted the relative speed at which modernization has taken place.

items: 2012Standoff at Bajo de Masinloc. Congress passes RA 10349 in December.
2013BRP Ramon Alcaraz commissioned
2016BRP Tarlac delivered, the program’s first major vessel
2020–2021BRP Jose Rizal and BRP Antonio Luna, the first brand-new frigates
2025BRP Miguel Malvar (summer) and BRP Diego Silang (December) commissioned
2027End of the program’s 15-year horizon

blocks.text: SILANG’S CHIEF. Captain John Percie Alcos is the first commanding officer of the BRP Diego Silang.
North, west, and everything in between
The AFP’s long-overdue modernization, to a large extent, was spurred by China.
In 2012, the Philippine Navy was in a brief standoff with Chinese maritime forces in Bajo de Masinloc (Scarborough Shoal).

By June that year, the Philippines eventually withdrew the white-hulled Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) vessel, expecting China to do the same under a deal supposedly brokered by the United States. Beijing stayed.

To this day, at least one China Coast Guard (CCG) ship is stationed at the opening of the shoal, with at least one or two more roving within its vicinity. Chinese Maritime Militia serve as force multipliers in Beijing’s sovereignty claim over the shoal.
In early December 2012, the Philippine Congress passed Republic Act No. 10349 or the Revised Armed Forces of the Philippines Modernization Program Act, a 15-year plan divided into three horizons.
READ FAST FACTS: Big ticket items in the Philippine Navy’s modernization

China’s actions and apparent aspirations in the West Philippine Sea, an area that includes the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone (EEZ) and features where it has sovereignty claims, is the most obvious priority in the military and the reason for the Navy’s shift in focus to external defense.
But the western front is only one of five critical spots that the Navy must cover, through its fleet, the Marines, and other units that monitor and detect potential threats.

To the east is the Pacific Ocean, with the yet-to-be-tapped Philippine Rise in the northeastern part of the country’s vast maritime area. The “bigger domain” east to the Philippines is where the military must “start building infrastructure and logistical bases,” said Teodoro in an August 2026 budget hearing.
Down south are both sea-lanes and porous borders between the southernmost Philippines and neighbors Malaysia and Indonesia.
NORTHBatanes and Taiwan
WESTWest Philippine Sea
EASTPacific Ocean, Philippine Rise
BETWEENArchipelagic sea-lanes
SOUTHSea-lanes, borders with Malaysia and Indonesia

Between the major island groups are archipelagic sea-lanes that are vital not only for domestic use but also for international trade and freedom of navigation. The Philippine Archipelagic Sea Lanes Act codified the 2016 Arbitral Award by identifying where foreign vessels, including the military kind, may pass.

Up north is where the AFP, non-uniformed experts, and pundits may feel the most anxious. Taiwan, an issue that for China is even touchier than the South China Sea, is a flashpoint for tensions not only between independently governed Taipei and Beijing, but the rest of the region.

Self-proclaimed Chinese scholars have claimed that the northernmost Batanes province is part of Taiwan and therefore, also China’s. The Chinese embassy in Manila, in September 2026, claimed “sovereign rights” over waters between Batanes and Taiwan.
Tensions over northernmost features started after the Philippines and Japan announced maritime delimitation talks.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has ruled out offensive attacks from the Philippines, even in the event of a Taiwan conflict. But the sheer proximity of the country’s northern provinces to Taiwan is also why Marcos has said that Manila would be dragged into the conflict “kicking and screaming.”

All of those potential flashpoints and weakpoints are where the Navy — the fleet, the Marines, and special units like the elite Special Warfare Force — is expected to always be on the frontlines and in the forefront.
READ Philippines tells China: Leave Panganiban, Zamora reefs in West PH Sea
It’s a tall order when budgets are perennially tight, assets remain limited to serve a vast archipelago, and resource gaps exist.
But as one officer once put it, the Navy and the rest of the armed forces have always managed to do the most with even the barest of means.
The western frontier

blocks.caption: NAVY WORKHORSE. The BRP Ramon Alcaraz (PS-41) is moored inside Ulugan Bay in Palawan in June 2025. Photo by Bea Cupin/Rappler

blocks.text: On most days, Ulugan Bay in Palawan is a picture of calm.

Tucked in the middle of Palawan island, the bay is close to the Western Command (Wescom) in Puerto Princesa City, the site of an air base where American troops may preposition assets under the bilateral Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement. It’s the center of West Philippine Sea operations for the Philippine military.

From Ulugan Bay, Pag-asa (Thitu) Island, the Philippines’ farthest civilian-populated island in the west, is just around a day’s sail away. It takes under two hours by military cargo plane to fly from Wescom’s Antonio Bautista Air Base to Rancudo Airfield in the remote island.

On a rainy June afternoon in 2024, the three vessels of the Del Pilar class — the BRP Gregorio del Pilar, the BRP Ramon Alcaraz, and the BRP Andres Bonifacio — were all moored in the middle of the bay as inclement weather slowly creeped into the Palawan mainland from the West Philippine Sea.

The Bonifacio had just narrowly missed bad weather in the West Philippine Sea after a weeklong Maritime Domain Awareness mission with reporters on board. The same weather conditions would cause a Chinese fishing vessel to run aground near Pag-asa (Thitu) Island.

The Del Pilar, former US Coast Guard cutters that were launched in the 1960s and commissioned into the Philippine Navy as frigates in 2011, 2013, and 2016, are the senior citizens of the Philippine Fleet.
They have since been upgraded beginning in the 2020s to more modern systems, as the South Korea-made frigates started arriving and the Del Pilar ships were reclassified as OPVs.

Dotting the shoreline of Ulugan Bay are private and public resorts and secluded homes — that is, until you get closer to Naval Detachment Oyster Bay, where smaller patrol ships, attack craft, and the Navy’s supply vessels are usually docked.
The detachment itself is surrounded by vast greenery.

In 2002, then-president Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo declared at least 1,838 hectares of land as part of the Ulugan Bay Naval Reservation, with most of it dedicated for what was then the proposed Naval Operating Base Ulugan.

More than two decades later, Oyster Bay is the site of major upgrades, thanks in part to the United States, treaty-ally of the Philippines. In 2025, the US announced several plans for the bay — a boat repair and maintenance facility, a fast boat base, and maintenance facility for unmanned surface vessels.

These planned upgrades are a huge boost to the capabilities of the Wescom, whose area of operation includes most of the West Philippine Sea — from the BRP Sierra Madre in Ayungin Shoal to Pag-asa (Thitu) Island, located beyond the country’s EEZ.

They’re part of the Navy’s “broader effort to strengthen the Armed Forces of the Philippines’ external defense capabilities, particularly its ability to sustain maritime operations in the West Philippine Sea,” said Navy public affairs chief Captain Marie Angelica Sisican in a message to Rappler.

Sisican, citing Teodoro’s earlier statements from 2024, said naval facilities on the western side of Palawan would “reduce the distance that naval assets would otherwise have to cover in conducting operations.”

US-funded projects, including the boat maintenance facilities, are “intended to enhance the [Philippine Navy’s] repair and maintenance capabilities for watercraft, including unmanned surface vessels, while improving existing infrastructure.”
The facility will cater to both the AFP and the PCG for “capabilities related to maritime security, maritime domain awareness, interoperability, and infrastructure development.”
Indeed, it’s the Wescom in Palawan and the Northern Command up north that have become the focus of US assistance.

America’s “once-in-a-generation investment” was first announced in 2024, a total of $500 million in foreign military financing for the Philippines. This has since grown to a $2.5-billion commitment in military aid over five years, from 2026 to 2030, under the US 2026 National Defense Authorization Act signed in December 2025.
2024 · Foreign military financing$500 million
2026–2030 · US 2026 NDAA$2.5 billion

The support for the US-Philippine alliance is one of the bipartisan issues in a deeply divided Washington, an indication not just of shared values but of common strategic interests. Even as US President Donald Trump has signaled a “strategic stability” with China, America still wants a “favorable, but durable, balance of power in which no state — including China — can impose its hegemony and hold the security or prosperity of our nation and our allies in question,” said US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at the Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore in May 2026.
READ No alibis: Retooling and modernizing the Marines

But even with bipartisan support for aid to fund the Philippines’ military upgrades, the White House’s message for partners and especially allies is clear: burdens must be shared. “Alliances only work when they are true partnerships. It is a two-way street. You don't have a strong alliance unless everyone has skin in the game. No freeloading,” said Hegseth in Singapore.
The Navy’s latest warship

blocks.caption: RADIO CHALLENGE. The BRP Diego Silang (FFG-7) issues a radio challenge to a Chinese warship that was tailing it during an August 2026 multilateral joint sail in the West Philippine Sea. Photo from AFP PAO

blocks.text: At the bridge of the BRP Diego Silang, a junior officer was calm as she pored over the lines that she would repeat many times over in the coming hour or so.

It was August 22, 2026, and a Chinese navy ship sailed nearby, some 7 nautical miles away, as the Silang headed to a point in Escoda (Sabina) Shoal for a maritime patrol and a joint sail with Australia and the United States. The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) Navy ship had been trailing the Silang since the day prior.
It was her turn, as the junior officer on duty, to issue Silang's challenge to the interloper.

Before she could settle into her station, the speakers crackled. From it, the bridge heard the slow and deliberate voice of a Chinese sailor claiming Beijing’s "indisputable sovereignty” over Escoda Shoal, a low-tide feature where sovereignty cannot be claimed.
It was the Chinese warship’s first response to the Silang after previous challenges went unanswered.

The junior officer and the rest of the crew were unperturbed. She picked up a phone handset and spoke deliberately. It was her voice that the bridge over at the Chinese navy ship heard. “PLA Navy 536, this is Philippine Navy warship 7. You are a state party to UNCLOS. You are endangering our security. Leave the vicinity immediately — over.”

The August 2026 exercise was just one of many the Silang has been part of since its commissioning in December 2025. There has been little rest — after its first exercise in Philippine waters was a long sojourn to Australia for the multilateral naval exercise Kakadu. Between drills with allied and partner navies, it spent a few weeks out at sea to safeguard a regional meeting.

Alcos, during the five-day mission at sea, showed some signs of tiredness, even as he was quick to say the pace of engagements is one that he welcomes. The Silang’s crew, especially its officers, are young and eager to learn.

Some had been assigned to older warships, a few more to the Rizal or the Malvar. Other personnel of the Silang may soon man the newly arrived OPVs. From her crew could be the future commanding officers of modern platforms — frigates, landing platform docks, or OPVs that are forthcoming.

At around 6:30 in the evening, the speaker system of the Silang crackled again — this time, for prayer that was slowly and deliberately recited for all of its crew to hear. Most of the lines were standard fare, but a few were specific to a soldier’s life.

“Ipagtanggol mo kami sa karahasan ng mga kalaban (Defend us from the enemy’s violent ways).” The short prayer also asked God to save the Silang’s crew and their comrades in the Navy from disaster and other harms out at sea.

In the vastness of the West Philippine Sea, faith is essential — in a God who looks after a ship and her crew, in skills that her officers have earned and honed through the years, and in a steadfast commitment to defend what Filipinos have always known is theirs. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Family of Indigenous woman found dead in Melbourne mourn ‘vibrant, beautiful young girl’
articles.summary:
Police have charged a 31-year-old man with the alleged murder of Jayda Allen Bonner, whose body was found in a Carlton apartment on Saturday

  • Follow our

blocks.text: The family of a young Indigenous woman found dead in an apartment complex in Melbourne’s inner-north on Saturday say they are “absolutely crushed and shattered” by her death.
Jayda Allen Bonner, 21, was found dead on the fifth floor of an apartment block on Cardigan Street, Carlton on Saturday at about 1.45am.
Police on Wednesday charged a 31-year-old man with murder. He was expected to appear in the Melbourne magistrates court that afternoon.
The man presented himself at a police station on Monday, police said.
A 60-year-old man who was initially arrested has been released without charge.
Bonner’s aunt, Kellie Carter-Bell described her niece as a “vibrant, beautiful young girl” who was “fed to the wolves because the system didn’t listen”.
Carter-Bell said Bonner had been with her partner, who was 10 years her senior, since she was 15 years old.
Bonner lived with Carter-Bell in Melbourne as a young child and attended school in Carlton.

blocks.caption: A memorial outside the Cardigan Street apartment where Jayda Allen Bonner was found dead. Photograph: Joel Carrett/AAP

blocks.text: Her aunt said “she was a beautiful family girl”, who had hopes of moving back to Queensland to be with “her mob and to work in the community”.
“Jayda wanted to share her own knowledge of what she could [do] to help her community,” she said. “I’ve heard from her school teachers what a beautiful, vibrant young lady she was.

“She had a lot of dreams and aspirations … She looks exactly like her mother, which is beautiful.
“She’s someone this world shouldn’t have lost.
“I couldn’t save my niece, so I feel worthless and useless at the moment.
“The family is absolutely crushed and shattered “We don’t want her to ever be forgotten.”

articles.title: Sara Duterte camp says NBI's Matibag 'politically biased' vs. VP
articles.summary: The camp of Vice President Sara Duterte claimed Wednesday that National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag is "evidently politically biased" against her amid the investigation into…

blocks.text: Published October 14, 2026 11:11am

The camp of Vice President Sara Duterte claimed Wednesday that National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag is "evidently politically biased" against her amid the investigation into the allegations of dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr.
Citing the Vice President, Atty. Paul Lawrence Lim said that Matibag "is heavily burdened with a conflict of interest" in his investigation into Gracioso's accusations.

"As shown in the impeachment case, Director Matibag has previously written scathing opinion articles against the Vice President, and is evidently politically biased against her," Lim said in a statement.

"With respect, his current publicity on the progress of what is supposed to be a live investigation—showing support for Mr. Gracioso and implying guilt to the Vice President and her family, simultaneous with the impeachment trial—appears to confirm this bias," he added.
Duterte's lawyer said the NBI should not be weaponized for partisan purposes as it is expected to conduct professional and apolitical investigative work.
GMA News Online reached out to the NBI for a comment and will update this story once it responds.
Matibag earlier said the bureau is investigating properties supposedly linked to the vice president and her family to follow a pattern that was established in the affidavit of Gracioso.

The dismissed policeman has claimed that he delivered suitcases full of cash to the Vice President, Davao City Representative Paolo "Pulong" Duterte, and former president Rodrigo Duterte on the instructions of former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
The Dutertes have denied the claims of Gracioso, while Velasco's camp also said the alleged "fabricated attacks" against him have "no basis."
On Tuesday, the vice president has denied ownership of the properties being investigated by the NBI, saying that the move to associate them to her was a kind of "public deception."
The NBI earlier said it has invited Paolo Duterte to shed light on Gracioso's claims, an invite which he dismissed.
In his affidavit, Paolo Duterte said Gracioso's allegations were "pure fiction" and a "fairy-tale lie." — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: ICC rejects Duterte camp bid to cap evidence at 10,000 items
articles.summary: The International Criminal Court has rejected former president Rodrigo Duterte’s defense team’s request to limit the prosecution’s evidence to 10,000 items in his crimes against…

blocks.text: Headlines
October 14, 2026 | 11:03am
Former president Rodrigo Duterte attends the fourth status conference at the International Criminal Court in The Hague, Netherlands, on Oct. 13, 2026.
International Criminal Court / Philstar.com's screenshot

MANILA, Philippines — The International Criminal Court (ICC) has rejected former president Rodrigo Duterte’s defense team’s request to limit the prosecution’s evidence to 10,000 items in his crimes against humanity of murder case over killings linked to his administration’s anti-drug campaign.

Duterte attended the fourth status conference on Tuesday, October 13, as the ICC Trial Chamber III denied the defense’s request for the prosecution to refile its evidence in a new case file in the Judicial Workflow Platform (JWP), the court’s digital system for managing case records and evidence.
“Your motion that the evidence should be refiled in JWP and the prosecution limited to 10,000 documents is at the moment refused,” Korner said.

Korner said the proposed new case file and evidence cap could violate the prosecution’s disclosure obligations. She advised prosecutors to identify exculpatory evidence and urged Duterte’s lead counsel, Peter Haynes, to provide search terms to help locate materials relevant to the defense.
Haynes said he and prosecutor Julian Nicholls had maintained regular communication and cooperation in handling the case.
Nicholls, however, said prosecutors had asked the defense for search terms but had yet to receive them.

He proposed appointing an independent expert to review the evidence and suggested that both sides agree on documents confirming deaths during police operations to establish the number of killings reflected in the dataset without examining every document.
Evidence dispute

In a motion filed in September, Duterte’s defense team asked the ICC to cap the prosecution’s evidence at 10,000 items, arguing that the volume of materials disclosed ahead of trial would hamper its preparation.

The defense said the prosecution’s evidence had grown from 5,275 items during the confirmation phase to 62,130 items. It also cited more than 320,000 pages of documents and 1,000 audio-visual materials.

The status conference came after the ICC ruled that Duterte was fit to stand trial. The tribunal’s decision, made public on October 8, cleared the way for the proceedings to begin as scheduled on November 30.

Duterte faces three counts of crimes against humanity involving alleged murders and attempted murders committed in the Philippines between November 2011 and March 2019, according to the charges filed by prosecutors.
The case stems from the ICC’s investigation into alleged crimes against humanity linked to killings during Duterte’s anti-drug campaign.
Duterte was arrested in Manila in March 2025 and surrendered to the ICC on March 12, 2025. He remains detained at the ICC Detention Centre in Scheveningen, The Hague, Netherlands.

articles.title: LIVE UPDATES: Impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte
articles.summary: Bookmark this page for Rappler's comprehensive coverage of Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial at the Senate

blocks.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

There are four articles of impeachment against Duterte involving alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Only 21 out of 24 senator-judges are physically present. Senator Bato dela Rosa remains in hiding as he faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Senator Jinggoy Estrada has been detained and suspended in connection with a plunder case, and Senator Rodante Marcoleta surrendered to authorities as he also faces a plunder case.
On this page, we bring you the latest updates, analyses, videos, and photos as the trial of the Vice President unfolds.

articles.title: Visayas, Mindanao may expect rains due to ITCZ — PAGASA
articles.summary: In its weather forecast on Wednesday, October 14, PAGASA said that Visayas and Mindanao may expect cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms due to the ITCZ.

blocks.text: October 14, 2026 | 10:18am
Commuters and motorists brave heavy rains along United Nations Avenue in Manila.
The STAR / Ryan Baldemor
MANILA, Philippines — Visayas and Mindanao may experience rains due to the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), the state weather bureau PAGASA said.
In its weather forecast on Wednesday, October 14, PAGASA said that Visayas and Mindanao may expect cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms due to the ITCZ.
The state weather bureau warned residents of these areas of possible flash floods or landslides due to moderate to, at times, heavy rains.
Meanwhile, Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region and Cagayan Valley may expect partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated light rains due to northeasterly windflow.
Metro Manila and the rest of Luzon may also expect partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rain showers or thunderstorms due to localized thunderstorms.
PAGASA also reported that it is monitoring a tropical depression outside of the Philippine area of responsibility.
The weather system is estimated to be at 2,340 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon, as of 3 a.m. on Monday.

articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon trial shown crime scene reconstruction as ballistics expert traces bullet trajectories
articles.summary:
3D computer video of Paddington terrace shown to jurors outlines prosecution version of alleged murders of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies

A computer-generated reconstruction of the alleged…

blocks.text: A computer-generated reconstruction of the alleged double murder of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies has been played to a Sydney jury, as pictures showing gun marks on a bedroom door were examined by the supreme court.
Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of shooting dead the Sydney couple with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.
The defence has argued the couple were accidentally shot in two separate struggles and Lamarre-Condon acted in self-defence.
The prosecution has told the court that Lamarre-Condon shot Baird twice in the kitchen before shooting Davies through a bedroom door.
A computer-generated video outlining the crown’s version of events was played to the New South Wales supreme court jury on Wednesday.

A 3D recreation of the Paddington terrace on the night of the shootings allowed the jury to see the alleged path Lamarre-Condon took through the home. The reconstruction included photos of bullet holes and marks.
The potential trajectory of the bullets was also highlighted.
Before the video was shown, justice Natalie Adams said it was the crown case that Baird was shot at close range but the defence argued he was shot from further away.
The judge warned the kitchen was not shown to scale and that not all the evidence relevant to the angle or distance of the shot to Baird’s head had been adduced.
The NSW police firearms examiner Lucas Van Der Walt said he was more certain of the trajectory of the bullet through the bedroom door because it had passed 35mm thick wood.
Van Der Walt told the court that “stippling” had been found on the door around a bullet hole that the prosecution alleged was covered with putty and a plastic hook.
Stippling is the pattern made by gun shot propellant particles. The closer a target is to a barrel, the smaller the spread pattern would be, Van Der Walt said on Wednesday.
“[It] is going to pepper itself into that softer surface – in this case a painted door,” he told the jury.
The court was shown a video of police taking the door from Baird’s bedroom and shooting it with the same gun and ammunition that was allegedly used by Lamarre-Condon.

The pictures of both the original and test bullet hole were compared and shown to the jury. Van Der Walt said there was a “very similar spread pattern of the propellant particles impacting with the paint and the wood in the door”.
He suggested the muzzle of the firearm was 10 to 20cm away from Davies when it was discharged.
On the side of the door the bullet would have exited, he noted the splintering looked more opaque in the original hole, but he said that was because wood putty had been used to fill the hole.
Asked why there was no other bullet marks or bullets found in the room, the expert said it could have hit a hypothetical pillow, jacket or similar item.
“If that bullet continued and penetrated any of these surfaces and that object was removed and discarded, we’ll never find that bullet,” he told the court.
“If it slowed down enough and it only lightly impacts with a surface, it might leave behind a scuff mark that’s not convincing that it’s a bullet impacting – it might look like normal wear and tear.”
Bullets shot in this way fell to the ground, he said, and given the scene had been cleaned extensively, a casing could have been picked up by cleaners, Van Der Walt told the jury.
The trial before justice Adams continues.

articles.title: WATCH: ICC prosecutor defends data on 3,400 deaths in Duterte drug war
articles.summary: During a status conference on Tuesday, Nicholls disputed the defense’s claims about the dataset, saying the prosecution separated deaths in police operations from other killings included in the…

blocks.text: October 14, 2026 | 10:14am

MANILA, Philippines — International Criminal Court (ICC) senior trial lawyer Julian Nicholls pushed back against former president Rodrigo Duterte’s defense after it questioned the reliability of the prosecution’s data on drug war killings, insisting that analysts manually reviewed the records used to identify around 3,400 deaths in police operations.

During a status conference on Tuesday, Nicholls disputed the defense’s claims about the dataset, saying the prosecution separated deaths in police operations from other killings included in the larger collection of documents.

Duterte is facing three counts of crimes against humanity involving murder and attempted murder allegedly committed as part of a widespread and systematic attack against civilians in the Philippines between Nov. 1, 2011, and March 16, 2019, in the context of the government’s war on drugs.
The trial is scheduled to begin on Nov. 30, 2026, following an ICC ruling that the former Philippine leader is fit to stand trial.

articles.title: Lena Dunham's Girls to return for limited HBO run
articles.summary: Ten years after the series finale, the "Girls" are getting back together to explore the "milestone of turning forty", HBO says.

blocks.text: HBO's award-winning show Girls will return to screens for a limited run ten years after the series finale aired.

Lena Dunham – the show's creator, writer, and one of its stars – shared the announcement in a mock zoom call with members of the original cast Allison Williams, Jemima Kirke, Zosia Mamet and Andrew Rannells.

All five actors, whose careers launched off the back of Girls, will be part of the five-episode revival with production set to begin in 2027. Judd Apatow, who helped get the show green lit with HBO, will also return as executive producer.
"We always said we would only return to 'Girls' if there was a specific story we were burning to tell," Dunham said in a statement.
"I've missed these characters, but for a long time I couldn't quite picture them in the present day," she said.
"Then, right around my 40th birthday, they started talking to me in the shower. And, as you may remember, once this fivesome starts talking it's pretty hard to get them to stop," she said.
Girls, which ran for six seasons from 2012 to 2017, was nominated for 19 Emmys and won two, including best casting.
It follows the lives of four friends – Hannah, played by Dunham, Marnie, played by Williams, Jessa, played by Kirke and Shoshanna, played by Mamet – living in New York City during their 20s.
The show, created by Dunham when she was 23-years-old, attracted both praise and controversy during its airing. The BBC ranked it as number 30 on its 100 Greatest TV Shows of the 21st Century.
"We're thrilled to have Lena turn her gaze from the tumult of one's twenties to the milestone of turning forty," Amy Gravitt, executive vice-president of HBO programming, said.

"To say the world has changed since we last saw Hannah, Marnie, Shoshanna, Jessa, and Elijah is a massive understatement, but we know fans - old and new - will be happy to see how they've grown and relieved to see that they're still the 'Girls' we knew way back when."
The title of the limited run has yet to be announced, but Dunham did ask her fellow cast on the mock zoom call, "can we still call it Girls?", before joking "because we're old as".
Other cast and production members, most notably actor Adam Driver, were absent from HBO's official statement. Driver, in his breakout role, played Dunham's on-and-off again love interest in the show.
In her 2026 bestselling memoir Famesick, Dunham alleged Driver's on-set behaviour at times turned verbally aggressive and physically imposing. Driver has not publicly commented on the allegations.

In Famesick, Dunham also wrote about the breakdown of her working relationship and friendship with co-showrunner and executive producer Jenni Konner. Konner is not included in HBO's statement about the show's revival.
Dunham wrote on her Substack that "it's rare in life that you get the chance to return to something you love with new knowledge and a ... ton of gratitude.
"I love these girls (and boy) and I love all the people who have reminded us afresh why we do this, which is the joy of being together and the chance to wear yellow mesh…" she wrote.
Since Girls ended, Dunham has gone on to create the Netflix series Too Much in 2025 and indie film Sharp Stick.

articles.title: ’How do you explain the deletion of 130 million names?’ Why Indian voters are on the streets
articles.summary:
Anger at electoral roll changes has boiled over, sparking a crisis for Narendra Modi’s Hindu nationalist government

Born into a small village in West Bengal, Shahida Fakir had always taken…
articles.byline: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Shaikh Azizur Rahman

blocks.text: Born into a small village in West Bengal, Shahida Fakir had always taken her vote for granted. That was, until it was suddenly taken away. She presented officials with her Indian birth certificate and family land documents from the village going back to 1962.
Both her parents had been on the electoral roll going back decades, so she showed proof of that too. But when the final revised voter list came out in April, Fakir was not on it.

The 38-year-old migrant worker, born into a poor Muslim family, was not alone. Since last year, 130 million names – more than the population of Japan – have been removed from India’s electoral roll through a process known as SIR, or special intensive revision. In the nearly eight decades since India’s independence, never have the voter rolls shrunk by such a huge amount over such a short time.

blocks.caption: Shahida Fakir is staying in a village in Bangladesh after she was detained on suspicion of being an illegal immigrant and pushed across the border. Photograph: Supplied

blocks.text: The Narendra Modi government has called SIR a legitimate exercise to clean up the electoral rolls. Overseen by the election commission, tens of millions of dead and duplicate names have been removed. Yet so have the names of millions of living Indian citizens.

Critics allege that the pledge to “purify” India’s voter roll of illegal immigrants has instead been used for more sinister purposes – disenfranchising tens of millions of Muslims, other minorities, and poor and lower caste communities, who are largely not BJP voters.

In a matter of weeks, nationwide anger at SIR has boiled up and spilled out on to the streets of India’s biggest cities, presenting a formidable challenge to the government. Over the weekend, Delhi was transformed into a high-security fortress of barricades, roadblocks and tens of thousands of police and paramilitaries who detained thousands of people, as they attempted to stop youth-led protests calling for the man who oversaw SIR, the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, to step down immediately.

On Monday, opposition parties – who have decried SIR as a “weapon for vote theft” by the Modi government – drew tens of thousands of supporters as they marched through the capital and presented a petition to the supreme court, demanding Kumar’s resignation. The youth-led Cockroach Janta party (CJP) movement, who were behind the call for Saturday’s action, have vowed to “fight on” in their protests against SIR.

Opposition and civil society leaders allege that SIR has already given the BJP an electoral advantage in states such as Bihar and West Bengal, claims the party denied. Others say the exercise has had even more concerning implications: under changes to SIR unilaterally implemented by Kumar, the election commission has become the arbiter of Indian citizenship, a sweeping overreach of its remit.

The consequences are already playing out in West Bengal, where Modi’s Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) recently came to power and began a crackdown on “illegal” immigrants, complete with several new detention centres. Civil society groups say Muslims excluded by SIR are being targeted.

Fakir was among them. Just three months after the voter list was published – and while her hearing to challenge her exclusion was pending – she was picked up by police and accused of being an illegal Bangladeshi immigrant.

In July she was pushed over the border to Bangladesh, a country she had never been to nor had any connection with, and remains stuck there. “I have all the documents to prove I am an Indian citizen,” she said in a tearful phone call from the Bangladesh border village where she has been sheltering. “I fell on their feet and begged the police not to send me to Bangladesh but they pushed me over the border.”

blocks.caption: A protest march in Dhaka, Bangladesh, against India’s ‘push-ins’ of Muslims at the border in June. Photograph: Mamunur Rashid/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

blocks.text: A Bangladesh border guard officer confirmed Fakir’s account. “We checked all her documents and are convinced that she is an Indian citizen,” they said. In September, her family submitted a petition to the supreme court challenging her deportation. The Indian government was given a month to respond.

“All I want is to return to my family and my home in India. I am waiting desperately for that day,” she said. The backlog of millions of voters in West Bengal challenging their exclusion means it could be years before Fakir’s case is heard.

Those across West Bengal who have been stripped of their votes speak of their terror of being accused of being an alien in their own land. Some have had benefits taken away. Mohammad Hedayet Ullah Siddiqui, 80, from the North 24 Parganas district, said his grandfather had been a freedom fighter for Indian independence and three generations of his family were on the voter rolls. Yet after SIR, Siddiqui described his “humiliation” on finding his name gone.

“With my name erased from the voter list, I am in constant terror. What if they send me to a detention camp?” he said. “I cannot bear to think about being separated from my children and grandchildren at this age, especially when all my ancestors have been buried in India.”

blocks.caption: BJP supporters celebrate during vote counting at state elections in West Bengal in May 2026. Photograph: Dibyangshu Sarkar/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Critics say the problems began in 2023, when the Modi government changed the process for appointing the three-body election commission, giving majority control to the government for the first time. Within a matter of months, the Modi-led panel had appointed Kumar as the election commissioner in spite of opposition objections.
after newsletter promotion

“For decades, the election commission was one of our more credible, independent bodies, but now that has been eroded,” said Ronojoy Sen, a senior fellow at the South Asian Studies Programme, National University of Singapore.

By the following year, the new election commission body had begun SIR, starting in Bihar, where it immediately raised concerns among human rights groups after more than 6 million names were removed. Not long after the revisions, the BJP won a landslide victory in the Bihar state elections.

Despite concerns over SIR rumbling on for months, it did not spark national protests until the Indian Express newspaper last month revealed that two members of the election commission had raised 14 objections to how voters were being excluded from the rolls, but they were unilaterally overruled by Kumar.

“India has always been a flawed democracy but at least citizens felt they had the right to vote and that elections were regular and fair,” said Sen. “SIR has taken away that right. From how it has been conducted, it’s difficult to see how the motive was anything other than to enhance the election prospects of the BJP.”

Three former election commissioners have openly criticised SIR as a “hostile exercise” that has undermined the sanctity of the country’s electoral rolls by focusing on the exclusion – rather than inclusion – of voters. OP Rawat, a former chief election commissioner, described changes to the voter registration form as “wrong and illegal”.

Ashok Lavasa, who was an election commissioner between 2018 and 2020, called for the SIR to be scrapped. “An unfair procedure has been imposed on millions of people in the country, and you have the judiciary which has validated that,” he said last month. “How do you explain the deletion of 130 million names?”

None have been more vehement in their opposition than SY Qureshi, who was chief election commissioner between 2010 and 2012. “This is a national harassment exercise designed to throw Muslims off the electoral roll,” he claimed. “The only way to restore the credibility of India’s elections is to restore those deleted voters.”

The BJP has denied any political involvement or motive in the SIR process, accusing the opposition Congress party of “jealousy” over its recent electoral victories and saying any deleted voters can simply re-enrol. The BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi said the allegations were “disinformation” and part of an opposition campaign “being orchestrated to create an atmosphere of division and anarchy”.

Nonetheless, the election commission has appeared to accept some flaws in the process. Late last week, it belatedly put a cap on the number of voter deletion forms – which allow people to submit objections on behalf of others – after incidents in which people submitted thousands of forms targeting legitimate Muslim voters.
Public anger, meanwhile, has continued to build. In Delhi, where the SIR exercise left millions of people off the draft list, protests are expected to continue this week.

A Delhi resident for 30 years, Prashant Tandon, 60, said he could not believe it when a notice came to his door, questioning his life as a voter. “If someone doubts my citizenship, they should produce evidence against me,” he said furiously, adding that he would be protesting alongside the young people. “I should not have to prove that I am an Indian citizen.”
Additional reporting Aakash Hassan

articles.title: Bank of America hit with $1.2bn fine for money laundering failings
articles.summary: The bank inadequately flagged transactions linked to potential Chinese money laundering networks, the Treasury said.

blocks.text: Bank of America has been fined $1.2bn (£910m) for failing to detect potential money laundering and other illegal activity, the US Treasury Department said on Tuesday.
The banking giant failed to report over $5bn in suspicious activity to the government, $1bn of which posed national security and illicit finance risks, the Treasury said.

Those failures included not flagging transactions that possibly involved Chinese money laundering networks or trade-based laundering "with a substantial nexus to the southwest border", according to the Treasury.
"Our team is far along with and committed to completing the work required to address the issues raised by our regulators," Bank of America told the BBC.
The announcement came less 24 hours before Bank of America was due to announce its quarterly earnings on Wednesday morning.
"Our third-quarter results will include a non-tax-deductible charge of $1.2 billion impacting net income by approximately 17 cents per share," the bank said in an emailed statement.
"We have already dedicated substantial personnel and resources to our ongoing remediation efforts, and those costs are in the current expense base," it added.

In announcing the fine, the third-largest the department has ever imposed, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said: "When a bank of this size fails to meet its anti-money laundering and sanctions obligations, the consequences extend far beyond its own walls, exposing the entire US financial system to significant illicit finance risks."
The Treasury said the bank overly relied on inquiries from outside parties like law enforcement and other financial institutions instead of its own internal controls.
This meant that it "effectively outsourced to third parties a substantial portion of its proactive detection and reporting obligations," the department said.

As part of the settlement, Bank of America admitted that it "willfully violated" the Bank Secrecy Act by failing to maintain a compliant anti-money laundering programme, conduct required due diligence on foreign correspondent accounts and file suspicious activity reports, the Treasury said.
The $1.2bn fine included penalties imposed by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) and the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).
The OCC's $750m fine marked the biggest penalty it has ever levied.
OFAC said its settlement with the bank was tied to 475 apparent violations of sanctions programmes including those on Russia and Iran, narcotics, and global terrorism.
The settlement amount of $11.6m reflected the determination that Bank of America's apparent violations were "non-egregious", OFAC said.

articles.title: Court overturns Tanya Plibersek’s protection order which company says blocked controversial NSW goldmine
articles.summary:
Federal court overrules decision by former environment minister for the McPhillamys goldmine development at Blayney

The federal court has overturned a rare protection order issued by former…

blocks.text: The federal court has overturned a rare protection order issued by former environment minister Tanya Plibersek under Indigenous heritage legislation, which the company said effectively blocked a controversial goldmine in the central west of New South Wales.
Regis Resources challenged the decision by the former minister to issue the order in 2024 under section 10 of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Heritage Protection Act.
The Wiradyuri Traditional Owners Central West Aboriginal Corporation asked the minister to protect the headwaters and the springs of the Belubula River as a site central to creation stories.
The company said at the time the protection order, while affecting only part of the site and not the area intended to be mined, would make its McPhillamys goldmine development at Blayney unviable.
The order blocked the company from building a tailings dam in the headwaters of the Belubula River.
In a decision on Wednesday morning, Justice James Stellios ruled the order was invalid. The reasons for the court’s decision will be published on Friday.

According to the ABC, Stellios said on Wednesday the court’s decision and his reasons “say nothing about the merits of the claim ... whether it’s a significant area or under threat of injury or desecration ... those are matters within the authority of the minister ... not the jurisdiction of this court.”
At a three-day hearing last year, Regis Resources argued it had been denied procedural fairness and the government made errors in the process it followed before issuing the protection order.

The company’s lawyer, Perry Herzfeld SC, argued a blue-banded bee Dreaming story that influenced the government’s decision to protect the area was not raised until two years after the initial application for a section 10 order was made.

In a statement, the company said it anticipated the current environment minister, Murray Watt, “will be required to redetermine the application for a Section 10 Declaration, having regard to the relevant findings made by Justice Stellios in the judgment”.
“Today’s federal court judgment is a significant and welcome step forward for the McPhillamys Gold Project,” managing director Jim Beyer said.

“The judgment finding that the Section 10 Declaration is legally invalid vindicates the position we have held since the Declaration was made in August 2024, and we are extremely pleased the Court has agreed.”

Regis Resources said because any process to redetermine the protection order application could be protracted and “or for the outcome not to be in Regis’ favour”, the company was still pursing an alternative approach to the development.

The company said that plan would involve co-disposal of filtered processed ore and waste rock into a single facility – referred to as an Integrated Waste Landform – “and entirely avoids the area impacted by the declaration”.
“After considerable delay and uncertainty, and more than two years of time lost, we are eager to move forward,” Beyer said.

“We look forward to engaging constructively with the Department through the redetermination process, and to advance one of Australia’s largest undeveloped gold projects – one with the potential to deliver lasting economic and social benefits to the Central New South Wales region and our broader stakeholder community.”
Comment has been sought from Watt.
with AAP

articles.title: Sara Duterte camp: Withdrawal of 3 articles of impeachment means allegations 'lacked basis'
articles.summary: The camp of Vice President Sara Duterte on Wednesday said the prosecution's withdrawal of three articles of impeachment is an admission that the allegations hurled against her lacked basis from the…

blocks.text: Published October 14, 2026 9:32am Updated October 14, 2026 9:54am

The camp of Vice President Sara Duterte on Wednesday said the prosecution's withdrawal of three articles of impeachment on Tuesday is an admission that the allegations hurled against her lacked basis from the start.
"The withdrawal is an admission that the allegations lacked basis from the very beginning," Atty. Salvador Paolo Panelo Jr., spokesperson for Duterte, said in a statement.

"Yet, it is also an injustice and a denial of due process because it deprives the Vice President of the opportunity to confront these charges and present countervailing evidence in the proper forum, which is the Senate Impeachment Court," he said.
"More than that, it deprived her of the vindication of the acquittal she deserves if the Court ruled only on the basis of evidence and law," Panelo added.
The Senate impeachment court on Tuesday accepted the move by the House prosecution panel to withdraw three of the four Articles of Impeachment leveled against Duterte.

Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis "Chiz" Escudero made the ruling after the prosecution told the Senate court that it will no longer pursue the three Articles of Impeachment and will only retain one: Article 2 on amassing of unexplained wealth due to failure to disclose assets in the Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) and non-divestment of business interests despite Constitutional prohibition. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Grad student accused of trying to flee U.S. after police questioned her about alleged poisoning
articles.summary: A Wyoming microbiology graduate student from China has been arrested on accusations she poisoned the tea of a colleague who had pending patents, then tried to flee the U.S. after police questioned…

image.caption: A March 2012 file photo shows the University of Wyoming campus sign in Laramie, Wyo. (Andy Carpenean/Laramie Boomerang/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

A Wyoming microbiology graduate student from China has been arrested on accusations she poisoned the tea of a colleague who had pending patents, then tried to flee the U.S. after police questioned her.
Microbiology grad student alleged to have poisoned tea of University of Wyoming colleague

Aili Wang, 32, was arrested Oct. 6 at Los Angeles International Airport, where prosecutors allege she sought to return to China. With her were "multiple" laptops, electronic storage devices and documents now in the possession of police.

Investigators say Wang was seen on surveillance video rummaging through the desk of the alleged victim, who specialized in technology for disease treatment — research similar to work Wang had done in China.
Wang remained jailed without bail Tuesday in Los Angeles.

items: Woman at centre of Cornell gang-rape case was 'misled' about investigation, lawyer says

blocks.text: It's claimed the poison was first detected when the wife of the alleged victim and others tested water from the coffee maker he used to brew tea.
The microbiology professor overseeing both graduate students, Mark Gomelsky, said the accusations have left him reeling. He said he was uncertain if the alleged victim will fully recover.

"It's been disheartening, to say the least, to see that one of your student's life is in jeopardy and another student may be responsible for that," Gomelsky told The Associated Press. "That was one of the worst shocks in my professional career."
Wang has no attorney listed in court documents. The Associated Press tried to reach her via email and LinkedIn messages.
Surveillance in shared office space

The police investigation began after the victim, identified in court documents as K.T., began experiencing symptoms and his wife and others allegedly isolated the chemical acrylamide in the coffee maker's water.
K.T. and campus police then set up surveillance cameras in the office space he shared with Wang at the university in Laramie, Wyo.

Wang allegedly was recorded Sept. 27 going through K.T.'s desk. On Oct. 1, she was recorded "taking photos and manipulating notebooks" on his desk, as well as rinsing out his mug with a liquid from her own mug, a University of Wyoming campus police officer's affidavit said.

items: Disgraced former Manitoba law dean racked up millions in Swiss debt ahead of France arrest, documents suggest

blocks.text: Wang and the alleged victim, who did not share research areas, did not get along, according to the affidavit.
Police said Wang had asked eBay to delete her account after she bought acrylamide over the online retail site twice last summer.
A carcinogenic byproduct of cooking starchy food and burning tobacco, acrylamide, which can be acutely toxic in high doses, is also used in microbiology research involving proteins or DNA.
During an interview by campus police on Oct. 5, Wang allegedly said she "had not used acrylamide in years."

A day later she was taken into custody in Los Angeles while in possession of "multiple laptops, multiple portable external digital storage devices, related accessories, physical records and written materials," according to a request by Wyoming prosecutors to "significantly increase" her $200,000 US bond upon extradition.

Wang had no reason to go through the desk of the other student whose federally funded, patent-pending research involved "new technology for cancer, neurological and genetic disease treatment," according to the affidavit.
Wang "was reportedly working on similar research in China before coming to the U.S.," the affidavit alleges.
Envied colleague's success, prof says
Gomelsky described the alleged victim as a highly successful student from Vietnam.

Wang failed her first attempt to defend her dissertation and became envious of her colleague's success in discovering how to deliver RNA to human cells using bacteria, Gomelsky told The Associated Press.
The alleged victim began experiencing extreme tiredness, inability to sleep and other unexplained symptoms soon after attending a conference in August, Gomelsky said.
Later that month he went to the campus health clinic with worsening finger tingling and numbness, and leg weakness.
The student also said he had noticed a strange taste in the tea that he made with a small coffee maker on his desk, Gomelsky said, and that when he washed the coffee maker the taste would go away.
Suspecting someone in their shared office could be poisoning the student, Gomelsky said a chemistry professor tested the water and identified acrylamide.

The water from the coffee maker was boiled down to isolate 63 milligrams of white powder that tested positive for acrylamide, according to the affidavit. The amateur investigators turned the sample over to university police.
Unclear if alleged victim will recover

Discovery of the substance immediately made Tak Sumaya, an assistant professor who helped identify it in the coffee maker water, suspicious. Acrylamide is "not something you would find in that kind of quantity anywhere," Sumaya said.
The alleged victim was working on "a pretty promising cancer therapy method," Sumaya added.

items: 'An unfortunate accident': Calgary woman accused of killing security guard walks away from manslaughter charge

blocks.text: The alleged victim continues to experience symptoms from the poisoning, including not being able to focus, tiring easily and a loss of sensation in his left hand, Gomelsky said.
"Acrylamide is a neurotoxin that cannot be neutralized so it stays in neurons and basically kills them. So it's unclear if he'll fully recover or not," the professor said.
Wang faces a felony aggravated assault and battery charge in Wyoming punishable by up to 10 years in prison and a $10,000 US fine.
It's not clear when she could be extradited to the state, where Albany County Circuit Court Judge Robert Sanford granted prosecutors' request and raised bond to $1.5 million US, cash only.

articles.title: Russia detains Japanese journalist, accusing him of alleged spying
articles.summary:
FSB security agency said reporter was arrested on island of Sakhalin, alleging he was collecting information about Russia’s defences

Russia has arrested a Japanese journalist on the far east…

blocks.text: Russia has arrested a Japanese journalist on the far east island of Sakhalin and accused him of espionage, Moscow said on Tuesday.

Russia regards Japan as an “unfriendly” country because it has joined western sanctions over its war ⁠in Ukraine. Russia has arrested several citizens of “unfriendly” countries in recent years, accusing them of working for western intelligence services.

Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova identified the reporter as Yuki Imai from the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, saying Imai was accredited with the ministry but was accused of “conducting espionage activities on Russian territory”.
Japan’s embassy in Moscow told news agency Kyodo that the government was trying to ascertain the journalist’s reported detention.

Russia’s FSB security agency said a Japanese national, who it did not name, was arrested on Sakhalin and alleged he had worked for Japanese intelligence to collect information about Russia’s defences.

The FSB published a video showing masked officers storming a hotel room, pushing a man to the floor and handcuffing him. The man was flown to Moscow, where a court ordered he be held in pre-trial detention. It did not say when the arrest or court hearing occurred. The charges carry up to 20 years in prison.

Moscow and Tokyo have been locked in a territorial dispute for decades over the status of a string of islands in the Pacific Ocean, off the north-east coast of Japan and to the south-west of Russia’s Sakhalin region.
The FSB said it had “opened a criminal case against the Japanese national”, and that he had been placed in pre-trial detention, Russian news agencies reported, citing the agency.
Russian media reported he would remain in custody until 12 December.

“Attempts by Tokyo to use its correspondents in Russia … to gather information aimed at undermining the security of our state is regrettable,” Zakharova said, alleging this was “not an isolated case”.
The Kuril islands – which Japan calls the Northern Territories – have been under Russia’s control since the end of the second world war, when they were seized by the Soviet Union.

Russia’s president, Vladimir Putin, visited one of the disputed islands in August, causing an ​uproar in Japan. Tokyo has ‌said it would continue ​implementing sanctions against ​Russia and supporting Ukraine.
In 2023, US journalist Evan Gershkovich was arrested on espionage charges, later sentenced to 16 years in prison before being released in a 2024 prisoner swap.
With Agence France-Presse and Reuters

articles.title: What we know about the man who died falling from a Six Flags rollercoaster
articles.summary: Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem died on Monday after police say he was ejected from a ride at a Six Flags amusement park in Georgia.

blocks.text: The Cobb County Police Department said the incident at the Six Flags Over Georgia park happened just before 16:00 local time (20:00 GMT) on Monday.
"Officers working at the park responded to an incident involving a male guest on a roller coaster," it said in a statement on Tuesday.
"Preliminary information gathered through witness and employee interview indicates Kariem was ejected from the ride and struck other patrons before falling beneath the attraction."

The ride involved has not been specified but aerial footage from news helicopters showed the Goliath rollercoaster stopped midway, and multiple witnesses have identified the ride as the one involved in the incident.
The office of the state's insurance and fire safety commissioner, which enforces amusement park safety rules in Georgia, is also conducting a review.
Officials have not held a news conference on the incident.

The Goliath ride opened in 2006, and it has an elevation of 200ft (60m), a 170ft plunge, a 540-degree spiral, and a speed of up to 70mph (112km/h), according to the park website. On its "thrill scale", Six Flags ranks Goliath at level four out of five.
The company said in a statement that it was "deeply saddened by the guest incident" and that "our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends, and loved ones".
Nick Mendenhall said he witnessed the fatal moments in disbelief, watching the man come out of his seat and then fall into another cart on the ride before falling to the ground.
"It was just super, super bizarre, traumatic. I mean, it took me a couple of seconds, I feel like, to process what was going on," he told the AP. "I cant believe that I just saw that."
He said his mind instantly went to the trauma of all of those impacted by what he witnessed, including the man's loved ones and everyone who was on the ride with him.

One witness told NBC affiliate WXIA that the incident was captured in souvenir photos that were automatically taken of the rollercoaster while it was in motion. The BBC has not been able to verify this statement.
Connor Thompson told the BBC's US partner CBS News that he was in line for the ride when everyone started "yelling, clearly distressed".

"Everyone was kind of confused at first, and then there was someone who was yelling, 'Call 911! Someone fell out!" he said. "At first it was almost like I didn't believe it because I thought that was like impossible for something like that to happen."
He said he saw the cart come into the hub where others were waiting in line and could see the restraint was unlatched.
Another witness, CiCi Nelson, told CNN she, too, was in line to ride the Goliath when the rollercoaster returned and she saw an empty seat with a loose safety bar and a female covered in blood.
Nelson described a scene of hysteria, adding that one man was "freaking out, saying someone fell off".
Brittany Landry, who believed she saw Kariem ejected from the rollercoaster, told Fox News she was in tears.
"I broke because we were just on there," she said.
Kariem's family said he was a father, passionate educator and had survived two bouts of cancer.
His family told WXIA that he had survived cancer twice - the last stint in 2018 - and was in a car crash with his 10-year-old daughter three weeks before his death.
He lived in the nearby city of Atlanta and worked for Wesley International Academy, a public charter school, for more than 12 years as an IT manager, technology teacher and robotics coach.
"Mr. Kariem was deeply loved and respected, and his absence will be felt throughout our school community," the school said in a statement posted to its Facebook account.
"His love for Wesley, dedication to our students, and commitment to our school community were evident in everything he did."

Outside of work, Kariem enjoyed creating products with his laser engraver and 3D printers, as well as cooking, watching anime and spending time with family and friends, according to his profile on the school's website.
The death at Six Flags Over Georgia is at least the seventh there, according to the Doan Law Firm, which tracks amusement park accidents and represents victims.

According to the firm, this includes two people who had medical emergencies, two who were in restricted areas when they were struck by a ride, two who died in car-related accidents and one who died months after using the park's pool.
Six Flags operates 20 amusement parks, 14 water parks and nine resorts across Canada, the US and Mexico.

In the last 15 years, two deaths caused by falling from the park's rollercoasters led to lawsuits and settlements. One in 2011 involved an Iraq War veteran who was ejected from a ride in New York and hit his head on the car. In the other, in 2013, a woman slipped from her restraints on a rollercoaster in Texas and fell 75 feet.
In September, the Six Flags Magic Mountain park in California announced it was closing its X2 rollercoaster after more 100 people alleged that they had suffered brain injuries from the ride.
With additional reporting by Brandon Drenon

Wang allegedly asked eBay to delete her account after she bought acrylamide over the online retail site twice last summer, police said.
